How to sew a lined makeup bag with a zipper

A lined zipper bag from one rectangle of printed cotton, with a pink round corner at each end of the bottom. Watch it come together step by step.

Some links on this page are affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

Overview

The finished bag

A lined zipper bag for make-up, pencils and creams: printed cotton with thin interfacing, a pink round corner at each end of the bottom. Tap the bag to take it apart.

How it's done — Cut-out corners →

  1. 1Outer — printed cotton · 23 × 31 cm (9 × 12¼ in), folded in half: the fold is the bottom
  2. 2Interfacing — thin, fusible · 21 × 29 cm (8¼ × 11⅜ in), on the outer, 1 cm (⅜ in) from the edges
  3. 3Round corners ×2 — four pink pieces 18 × 10 cm (7⅛ × 3⅞ in) · half-circles of interfacing, radius 8 cm (3⅛ in), cut from a 16 × 16 cm (6¼ in) square
  4. 4Zipper — 20 cm (7⅞ in) · in the middle of the short sides, no topstitching
  5. 5Lining — cotton · 23 × 31 cm (9 × 12¼ in), without interfacing
  6. 6Seams — all 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) · a 6 cm (2⅜ in) opening in the lining, closed by hand · corners: 3.5 × 2.5 cm (1⅜ × 1 in) cut out

Step-by-step instructions

  1. From printed cotton cut the outer, 23 × 31 cm (9 × 12¼ in). Cut the lining the same size, 23 × 31 cm.

    From thin fusible interfacing cut a 21 × 29 cm (8¼ × 11⅜ in) piece for the outer and a 16 × 16 cm (6¼ × 6¼ in) square for the round corners.

    From pink cotton cut four pieces, 18 × 10 cm (7⅛ × 3⅞ in) — two for each corner.

    You also need a 20 cm (7⅞ in) zipper.

    Every seam allowance in this bag is 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in).

  2. Make a paper template: a circle with a radius of 8 cm (3⅛ in).

    Trace the circle on the 16 × 16 cm (6¼ in) square of interfacing and cut it out.

    Cut the circle in half: two half-circles, one for each round corner.

  3. Lay a half-circle of interfacing, glue side down, on the wrong side of a pink piece: in the middle, its straight side 1 cm (⅜ in) from one long edge. Iron it on.

    Put it on a second pink piece, right sides together.

    Sew along the curve, right on the edge of the interfacing.

    Make the second one the same way.

    Machine: straight stitch

  4. Cut away the extra fabric round the curve, leaving a narrow seam allowance.

    Notch the allowance along the curve so it lies flat.

    Turn both half-moons right side out through the straight side and press them. The straight side stays open.

  5. Lay the outer wrong side up.

    Place the interfacing on it, glue side down, 1 cm (⅜ in) in from every edge, and iron it on. The lining gets no interfacing.

    Fold the outer in half across its length and snip a small notch at both ends of the fold. The fold is the bottom of the bag — there is no seam there.

  6. Turn the outer right side up.

    Put a half-moon on each side edge: its straight raw edge level with the side edge of the outer, its middle on the notches — the bottom line.

    Stitch each one all round: along the curve right on the edge, along the straight side 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge. The straight side will go into the side seam.

    Machine: straight stitch

  7. Lay the outer right side up.

    Put the zipper face down along one 23 cm (9 in) side, in the middle: its ends stop short of the side edges, so they stay out of the side seams.

    Lay the lining on top, face down, its edge level with the outer.

    Sew through all the layers, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge. No topstitching along the zipper.

    Machine: straight stitch

  8. Open the lining out, away from the zipper.

    Fold the outer in half on the bottom line, right sides together, and the lining in half the same way.

    Their other short sides now meet the other side of the zipper: outer, zipper face down, lining — as before.

    Sew 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge. The outer and the lining are now one loop.

    Machine: straight stitch

  9. Open the zipper first: the bag will be turned out through it.

    Lay it flat, the outer right sides together on one side of the zipper, the lining on the other.

    Sew both side seams, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, through the half-moons too.

    In one side of the lining leave 6 cm (2⅜ in) open, in the middle of the seam.

    Machine: straight stitch

  10. Mark a 3.5 × 2.5 cm (1⅜ × 1 in) rectangle in each of the four bottom corners: 3.5 cm along the bottom, 2.5 cm along the side seam.

    Cut them out.

    Open each corner and flatten it so that the side seam lies on the bottom fold and the cut edges form one straight line.

    Sew straight across, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge. Do all four corners.

    Machine: straight stitch

    How it's done — Cut-out corners →

  11. Spread out the outer and the lining: the bottom and the corners stand up, and you have two shapes.

    The seams are on the outside and the open zipper sits between the two: the bag is still inside out.

  12. Pull the outer out through the opening in the lining and the open zipper.

    Tuck in the raw edges of the opening and sew it closed by hand.

    Push the lining into the bag, right into the corners, and close the zipper. The half-moons have turned into round pink corners.

Printed cotton for the outer and the lining, pink cotton for the corners, thin fusible interfacing, thread — and the tools I personally recommend for cutting, pressing and sewing it. You will also need a 20 cm (7⅞ in) zipper.

Good to know

Questions and answers

How much fabric do I need for a makeup bag?

For this bag you need a 23 × 31 cm (9 × 12¼ in) piece of printed cotton for the outer and one the same size for the lining, four 18 × 10 cm (7⅛ × 3⅞ in) pieces of pink cotton for the round corners, thin fusible interfacing — 21 × 29 cm (8¼ × 11⅜ in) and a 16 × 16 cm (6¼ in) square — and a 20 cm (7⅞ in) zipper. The cutting diagram below shows it all.

How do you sew a zipper into a lined pouch?

Lay the outer right side up, put the zipper face down along one short 23 cm (9 in) side, in the middle, and the lining face down on top. Sew through all the layers 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge. Then fold the outer and the lining in half so their other short sides meet the other side of the zipper, and sew it the same way. There is no topstitching along the zipper.

How do you make the corners of a makeup bag?

After the side seams, cut a 3.5 × 2.5 cm (1⅜ × 1 in) piece from each bottom corner — two on the outer, two on the lining: 3.5 cm along the bottom, 2.5 cm along the side seam. Open each corner so the side seam meets the bottom fold and sew straight across, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge.

How do you make the round corners?

Cut a circle of radius 8 cm (3⅛ in) from a 16 × 16 cm (6¼ in) square of interfacing, using a paper template, and cut it in half. Iron each half-circle onto a pink 18 × 10 cm (7⅛ × 3⅞ in) piece, its straight side 1 cm (⅜ in) from the long edge, sew it to a second pink piece along the curve, trim, notch and turn. Stitch the half-moons onto the side edges of the outer, their middle on the bottom line: once the corners are sewn, they turn into round pink corners.

Does a makeup bag need interfacing?

This one has thin fusible interfacing on the outer only: a 21 × 29 cm (8¼ × 11⅜ in) piece ironed onto the wrong side, 1 cm (⅜ in) from every edge. The lining has none.

Where do you leave the opening to turn it?

In the middle of one side seam of the lining: leave 6 cm (2⅜ in) unsewn, and open the zipper before you sew the side seams. Turn the bag right side out through the opening and the zipper, then close the opening by hand.
